issues.description: is_registered mutates the shared TritonLoraConfig — value and identity are complected, creating a race
issues.detail: TritonLoraConfig is treated as a value (returned from metadata, passed to request builders), but _create_trtllm_generate_request mutates lora_config.is_registered = True in place. Under concurrent requests two coroutines can both see False, both ship weights, or one can register while another assumes registration. Registration state is an identity-over-time fact about the server, not a field on the config value. Pull it out into an explicit registry keyed by name, or pass a value-plus-version.

issues.description: Auto-incrementing lora_task_id at parse time complects identity assignment with directory scanning
issues.detail: task_id is generated by a counter during _parse_lora_configs and then used as the TRT-LLM cache key. Across restarts, multiple repo paths, or reloads the same logical LoRA can get a different task_id, and a freshly-assigned id can collide with whatever the engine already cached. The task_id is an identity managed by the engine over time; deriving it from list order at parse time is place-oriented thinking. Derive it deterministically from the name, or get it from the backend.

issues.description: _parse_lora_configs complects vLLM and TRT-LLM discovery into one branchy function
issues.detail: The function now switches on backend to read model.json vs multi_lora.json, builds two different shapes of TritonLoraConfig, mixes exception semantics (ServerError re-raised, everything else swallowed to None), and reassigns lora_config_path as both a directory and a file path. That is three concerns in one body. Decompose into _parse_vllm_loras and _parse_trtllm_loras returning the same value type, with one shared repo-resolution helper.

issues.description: Swallowing all exceptions to None hides essential failures behind incidental ones
issues.detail: The outer except Exception still returns None, but now the body can raise from os.path.exists, np.load paths, or malformed JSON for TRT-LLM. Operators will see a LoRA-less model with no signal beyond a traceback printed to stdout. Distinguish "no LoRA configured" (value: None) from "LoRA configured but broken" (raise). Right now the two are complected.

issues.description: print(traceback.format_exc()) sprinkled across routers and parser is place-oriented logging
issues.detail: Four routers and the parser now print tracebacks to stdout. That is debugging scaffolding hardened into the code: it has no level, no logger, no structure, and will interleave with request output. Either route through the existing logger with a real level, or remove. "Easy" (print) is not "simple" (one logging concept).

issues.description: np.load happens inside the per-request path with no caching of the parsed arrays
issues.detail: The first request for each LoRA reads two .npy files from disk synchronously inside an async handler. The TritonLoraConfig already knows the path; the parsed weights/config are pure values keyed by path. Load them once at parse time (or memoize by path) and attach the arrays to the config. Re-reading on the hot path is incidental work driven by where the state lives, not by what the request needs.

review.summary: The change does a reasonable job carrying LoRA naming across two backends, but it complects three concerns that should be separated: the LoRA config value, the per-name identity (task_id), and the time-varying registration state with the engine. Mutating is_registered on a shared config under async request handling is a correctness bug, not a style point. The parser has also accumulated two backends, two failure modes, and a reused variable name in one body — decompose it. Debug prints in routers and the parser are easy-not-simple; route through the logger or delete. Think for a beat about what the value, identity, and time semantics of a LoRA actually are before shipping this surface.
